senses.gloss: A stiff flat board with a clip at the top for holding papers while you write.
examples: The nurse checked the chart on her *clipboard*.
A man with a *clipboard* was taking everyone's name at the door.
Two *clipboards* hung on a nail beside the shop door.

senses.gloss: A mixture of several different substances or factors, often a harmful one.
examples: Doctors put him on a *cocktail* of three drugs.
Runoff carried a *cocktail* of chemicals into the creek.
The crash was caused by a *cocktail* of fatigue, fog, and bad brakes.

senses.gloss: A cold appetizer of seafood or chopped fruit served in a small glass or dish.
examples: We ordered a shrimp *cocktail* to start.
She spooned fruit *cocktail* into little bowls for the kids.
The crab *cocktail* is listed under appetizers, not drinks.

senses.gloss: Someone who helps an enemy army that is occupying their country.
examples: After the war, *collaborators* were put on trial.
The resistance shot him as a *collaborator*.
Half the village accused the other half of being *collaborators*.

senses.gloss: A sudden and complete failure of a system, business, or plan.
examples: The *collapse* of the bank wiped out their savings.
Nobody at the firm predicted the *collapse* of the housing market.
The talks ended in *collapse* after three days.

senses.gloss: A group of objects of one kind that someone has gathered and keeps together.
examples: His stamp *collection* fills four albums.
The museum's *collection* includes two Rembrandts.
She left her record *collection* to the town library.

senses.gloss: Money gathered from a group of people for a church or a cause.
examples: They passed the plate for the Sunday *collection*.
The office took up a *collection* for her hospital bills.
The *collection* raised almost four hundred dollars.

senses.gloss: The regular picking up of trash or mail.
examples: Trash *collection* is on Tuesday mornings.
There is no mail *collection* on federal holidays.
The city moved recycling *collection* to every other week.

senses.gloss: An official whose job is to take in money that is owed or tickets that are due.
examples: A bill *collector* called the house twice a day.
The tax *collector* sent a final notice in April.
The ticket *collector* punched our stubs at the gate.

senses.gloss: A sharp clash between opposing ideas, groups, or interests.
examples: The hearing exposed a *collision* between science and politics.
The movie is about the *collision* of two very different cultures.
Their ambitions put the two men on a *collision* course.

senses.gloss: The series of numbers or letters that opens a lock.
examples: I forgot the *combination* to my gym locker.
The safe has a six-digit *combination*.
He changed the *combination* on the bike lock after it was stolen.

senses.gloss: A quick, clever reply to a remark or an insult.
examples: I thought of a great *comeback* about an hour too late.
Her *comeback* had the whole table laughing.
He is never short of a *comeback*.

senses.gloss: The beginning or start of something.
examples: Rent is due at the *commencement* of the lease.
Rain delayed the *commencement* of play by two hours.
Attendance is taken at the *commencement* of each class.

senses.gloss: An official group appointed to investigate something or to regulate an activity.
examples: A *commission* was set up to study the crash.
The planning *commission* meets on the first Thursday of the month.
Both *commissions* released their reports in the spring.

senses.gloss: A formal order for a piece of work, especially a work of art.
examples: She got a *commission* to paint a mural downtown.
The composer accepted a *commission* for a new symphony.
Most of his income comes from private *commissions*.

senses.gloss: Something useful or valuable, especially something that is in short supply.
examples: Time is the scarcest *commodity* in this house.
Trust is a rare *commodity* in that business.
Clean water became a precious *commodity* after the storm.

senses.gloss: A deep sharing of feeling, or a close bond with nature or with God.
examples: He hikes alone to feel some *communion* with nature.
The two writers lived in close *communion* for twenty years.
She described a quiet *communion* with the land she grew up on.

senses.gloss: The pay and benefits an employee receives for work.
examples: Her *compensation* package includes stock options.
The board voted to cut executive *compensation*.
Total *compensation* runs about ninety thousand a year.

senses.gloss: The people or companies that you are competing against.
examples: We have to price below the *competition*.
Our *competition* opened a second store on Main Street.
He studied the *competition* for a week before the tournament.

senses.gloss: Someone taking part in a contest or a race.
examples: Forty *competitors* signed up for the marathon.
The youngest *competitor* was eleven years old.
Each *competitor* gets three attempts at the bar.

senses.gloss: The full number of people or things needed to make something complete.
examples: The ship sailed with a full *complement* of crew.
The clinic is short of its usual *complement* of nurses.
A full *complement* of jurors was seated by noon.

senses.gloss: A forward pass that is caught, in American football.
examples: He had twenty-two *completions* in the game.
The drive opened with a thirty-yard *completion*.
The quarterback's *completions* dropped off in the second half.

senses.gloss: The parts or ingredients that make something up.
examples: The lab tested the chemical *composition* of the soil.
The *composition* of the committee changed after the election.
Scientists are studying the *composition* of distant planets.

senses.gloss: A fenced or walled area with a group of buildings inside it.
examples: Guards stood at the gate of the embassy *compound*.
The family lives in a *compound* a few miles outside town.
Trucks rolled into the *compound* at dawn.

senses.gloss: An idea or understanding of what something is or should be.
examples: He has no *conception* of how much a house costs.
Her *conception* of justice is not the same as mine.
The book challenges our whole *conception* of memory.

senses.gloss: A stand that sells food and drinks at a stadium, theater, or park.
senses.ru: киоск с едой и напитками (на стадионе, в кинотеатре)
examples: We got popcorn at the *concession* stand.
The *concessions* close at the end of the seventh inning.
Money from the *concession* pays for the team's uniforms.

senses.gloss: The end or final part of something.
examples: At the *conclusion* of the ceremony, everyone stood.
The trial reached its *conclusion* on Friday afternoon.
The *conclusion* of the book ties up every loose thread.

senses.gloss: A private matter told to someone you trust, or the trust that it will be kept secret.
examples: She told me in *confidence* that she is leaving in June.
He betrayed a *confidence* and lost a friend over it.
The two sisters traded *confidences* late into the night.

senses.gloss: Proof or an official statement that something is true.
examples: We are still waiting for *confirmation* of the death toll.
The photo was *confirmation* that he had been in the building.
Her account got *confirmation* from two other witnesses.

senses.gloss: A Christian ceremony in which a young person becomes a full member of the church.
examples: Her *confirmation* is on Sunday at ten o'clock.
He gave his nephew a Bible for his *confirmation*.
The whole family drove up for the *confirmation*.

senses.gloss: Official approval of a person appointed to a government post.
examples: The Senate scheduled *confirmation* hearings for June.
The nominee's *confirmation* passed by two votes.
*Confirmation* of the new chief took almost four months.

senses.gloss: A clash between two things arranged for the same time.
examples: I have a *conflict* on Tuesday at three.
We moved the meeting because of a scheduling *conflict*.
Check the calendar for *conflicts* before you book the room.

senses.gloss: Blockage of the nose or chest by mucus.
examples: This syrup helps with chest *congestion*.
She had *congestion* and a low fever for three days.
Nasal *congestion* kept him up half the night.

senses.gloss: A combination of two or more things happening or used together.
examples: The class is taught in *conjunction* with the state museum.
A *conjunction* of bad weather and low staffing closed the store.
The drug is used in *conjunction* with physical therapy.

senses.gloss: A person whose love or attention someone has won.
examples: He bragged to his friends about his latest *conquest*.
The novel lists his *conquests* in tiresome detail.
She had no interest in becoming another *conquest*.

senses.gloss: Awareness of a particular issue, or the shared ideas and feelings of a group.
examples: The campaign raised public *consciousness* about recycling.
Those songs shaped the national *consciousness* for a generation.
Class *consciousness* grew during the long strike.

senses.gloss: Importance or significance.
examples: It was a small matter of no *consequence*.
Nothing of *consequence* was said at the meeting.
The delay is of little *consequence* to us.
